questions.q: Why do major providers ship several sizes of the same model family instead of just one?
options: Larger models are always strictly worse, so smaller ones are a backup
Model size trades off directly against speed and cost, and no single size fits every task
Regulations require at least four models per provider
It's purely a marketing decision with no technical basis
questions.explain: Different tasks need different points on the speed/cost/capability trade-off, so providers ship a range of tiers rather than one-size-fits-all.

questions.q: Based on verified Anthropic pricing in this lesson, which tier is both the cheapest and fastest?
options: Claude Fable 5.1
Claude Opus 5.5
Claude Haiku 4.5
Claude Sonnet 5.5
questions.explain: Claude Haiku 4.5 is priced at $1/$5 per million tokens and described as the fastest tier — cheaper and faster than Sonnet, Opus, or Fable.

options: Always use the most expensive model available
Start with the fastest/cheapest model, test thoroughly, and upgrade only if there's a real capability gap
Never test a model before deploying it
Alternate randomly between models on every request
questions.explain: Efficiency-first means starting with the cheapest, fastest model and only moving up in tier once testing reveals it genuinely can't handle the task.

options: Start with the strongest model for a complex task, then look for room to downgrade once requirements are clear
Avoid flagship models entirely
Use the cheapest model only, regardless of task difficulty
Switch providers every time a new model launches
questions.explain: Capability-first means starting with the most capable model for a genuinely hard task, then optimizing toward efficiency once you understand what's actually required.

questions.q: Why might routing all of a high-volume customer-support chatbot's requests to a flagship model be a poor choice?
options: Flagship models cannot process customer support questions
It pays premium pricing and higher latency for capability most simple requests never needed
Flagship models refuse to answer simple questions
Customer support chatbots are not allowed to use large models
questions.explain: A flagship model's higher per-token cost and slower response time compound at high volume, often paying for capability that simple, repetitive requests don't actually require.
